The Chairman invited the Secretary to read the recommendation from the Appointments Committee. The Committee's report, dated 6th March 2021, reviewed three candidates:

a) Mr. Chinedu Okafor – Acting GM since January 2021. Previously served as Operations Manager (2018–2020). Holds a B.Sc. in Agricultural Economics from the University of Nigeria, Nsukka. The Committee noted his handling of the January fertilizer logistics crisis and his successful renegotiation of the warehouse lease.

b) Mrs. Patience Iorliam – External candidate, formerly with the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development in Abuja. Strong policy background but limited field experience in cooperative settings.

c) Mr. Andrew Kpande – Former branch manager with a private seed company in Kaduna. Good commercial record but did not submit full credentials before the Committee’s deadline.

The Committee recommended Mr. Okafor for the substantive role, citing his familiarity with OVCU operations and the positive feedback from staff and chapter leaders.

Discussion:
- Mrs. Felicia Ugbede asked whether Mr. Okafor’s appointment would be on the same terms as the previous GM. The Chairman confirmed that terms would be: 3-year contract renewable, salary grade GL 14 step 2, housing allowance included, and vehicle loan eligibility after 12 months.
- Mr. Emmanuel Tyodoo expressed concern about the timeline, noting that Mr. Okafor had not yet completed the full management training course sponsored by the Benue State Cooperative Federation. The Secretary confirmed that the course is scheduled for June 2021 and would not conflict with the appointment.
- Mrs. Grace Adanu asked about the Acting GM’s performance during the last two months. The Treasurer reported that the office had run smoothly and that Mr. Okafor had personally visited three chapters in February to resolve member disputes over seed distribution.

RESOLUTION:
It was moved by Mrs. Felicia Ugbede, seconded by Mr. David Aondoakaa, and resolved unanimously that:

Chinedu Okafor appointment_date 2021-03-15 date. Record status: current.

The appointment takes effect immediately. The Chairman is authorized to sign the letter of appointment and the contract deed. The Secretary is directed to communicate the decision to all chapters and to the Cooperative Federation office in Makurdi by 17th March.

The Board expressed appreciation to the Appointments Committee for their work and to Mr. Okafor for his service in the acting capacity.

- Total requirement: 2,400 bags (50kg each) of NPK 20:10:10
- Allocated to chapters: Ushongo 600, Logo 450, Guma 400, Vandeikya 350, Konshisha 300, Otukpo 300
- Estimated cost per bag: ₦9,500 (exclusive of transport)

The GM noted that the cooperative has secured a commitment from the Benue State Agricultural Development Authority for 1,200 bags at subsidized rate of ₦7,800 per bag. The remaining 1,200 bags will be purchased from open market.

---

- Mbayion's figure to be added when received; Planning Desk to call on Dec 29 and again on Jan 2 if no reply.

- Called Mbayion Cooperative Society twice; no answer. Left a message with the chairman's brother.
- F/O Zone C to visit Mbayion in person on Jan 3 if no reply by then.

**Dec 31 – Year-End Notes**

- Annual summary final version due today; Accounts to submit by 4:00 PM.
- All December trip logs were compiled; total trips: 11 (6 Zone A, 3 Zone B, 2 Zone C).
- Planning Officer to sign off on the annual report on Jan 2.
- Reminder: January calendar to be finalized by Jan 5; GM to approve after his return.

**OVCU Monthly Planning Log – January 2024**

---

**Jan 2 – Annual Report Sign-Off**

- Planning Officer reviewed and signed the 2023 annual report at 10:00 AM. Accounts had submitted the final version on Dec 31 at 3:45 PM, within the deadline.
- One correction was made before signing: the December fuel expense total was revised from N68,400 to N67,900 after Accounts rechecked the two logs with arithmetic errors (Dec 20 entries). The corrected figure is reflected in the final report.
- Membership table for 2023 was included as an annex. Kwande Cooperative Society listed membership_count_2023 as 180 members; this figure is current and was verified against the OVCU member records on Dec 28. All other societies matched the numbers previously circulated.

**Feb 6 – Staff Meeting**

- GM opened the meeting at 10:30 AM. Present: GM, Planning Officer, Accounts Officer, F/O Zone A, F/O Zone B, F/O Zone C. Apologies from the Admin Officer (sick).

---

**Apr 15 – Quarterly Audit Scheduling**

- Planning Desk confirmed with the external auditors (Messrs. Aondo & Associates, Makurdi) that the audit for Q1 2024 will commence on **May 6** and run through May 10. The audit date was set after the auditors confirmed availability; the earlier tentative date of Apr 29 was moved because the auditors had a prior engagement in Katsina-Ala that week.

  2. Receipts and payment vouchers, filed by month
  3. Membership contribution schedules
  4. Fertilizer sales records and warehouse issue notes
  5. Asset register with depreciation schedule
- The audit clearance (unqualified opinion) is required before the AGM financial report can be presented. GM reminded the committee that the previous year's audit was completed in three days; this year's scope is larger, so the extra day has been built in.
- Planning Desk to book a meeting room at the OVCU office for the audit team, and arrange for tea/refreshments. Accounts to confirm the petty cash float for incidental audit expenses (not to exceed N5,000 without prior approval).

- GM noted that the escalation agreed in February was not needed, and that the society's payment history should be noted as satisfactory for future credit requests.

---

**Apr 17 – Membership Updates (Final)**

- All 22 societies have now submitted their 2024 membership figures. Planning Desk consolidated the numbers and submitted the final summary to the GM on Apr 15. Total membership stands at 3,847 (up from 3,612 in 2023).
- Vandeikya Cooperative Society submitted the largest update (412 members); Lessel Cooperative Society submitted the smallest (98 members). The Lessel list was received on Apr 2, after two reminders.
- Planning Desk to prepare a one-page membership summary for the management committee meeting on Apr 24.

---

**Apr 18 – Training Kits Update**

- The training kits for Vandeikya members have not yet arrived. The supplier in Makurdi confirmed dispatch on Apr 3, but the courier company has not delivered. Planning Desk to call the courier today and request a tracking number.
- The refresher session scheduled for March was postponed; it will now be held on **May 15** at the Vandeikya Community Hall, subject to kit arrival. If the kits do not arrive by May 2, the session will be postponed again to June.

documents.title: OVCU Board Meeting Minutes
documents.content:
The Chairman invited the Secretary to read the recommendation from the Appointments Committee. The Committee's report, dated 6th March 2021, reviewed three candidates:

a) Mr. Chinedu Okafor – Acting GM since January 2021. Previously served as Operations Manager (2018–2020). Holds a B.Sc. in Agricultural Economics from the University of Nigeria, Nsukka. The Committee noted his handling of the January fertilizer logistics crisis and his successful renegotiation of the warehouse lease.

b) Mrs. Patience Iorliam – External candidate, formerly with the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development in Abuja. Strong policy background but limited field experience in cooperative settings.

c) Mr. Andrew Kpande – Former branch manager with a private seed company in Kaduna. Good commercial record but did not submit full credentials before the Committee’s deadline.

The Committee recommended Mr. Okafor for the substantive role, citing his familiarity with OVCU operations and the positive feedback from staff and chapter leaders.

Discussion:
- Mrs. Felicia Ugbede asked whether Mr. Okafor’s appointment would be on the same terms as the previous GM. The Chairman confirmed that terms would be: 3-year contract renewable, salary grade GL 14 step 2, housing allowance included, and vehicle loan eligibility after 12 months.
- Mr. Emmanuel Tyodoo expressed concern about the timeline, noting that Mr. Okafor had not yet completed the full management training course sponsored by the Benue State Cooperative Federation. The Secretary confirmed that the course is scheduled for June 2021 and would not conflict with the appointment.
- Mrs. Grace Adanu asked about the Acting GM’s performance during the last two months. The Treasurer reported that the office had run smoothly and that Mr. Okafor had personally visited three chapters in February to resolve member disputes over seed distribution.

RESOLUTION:
It was moved by Mrs. Felicia Ugbede, seconded by Mr. David Aondoakaa, and resolved unanimously that:

Chinedu Okafor appointment_date 2021-03-15 date. Record status: current.

The appointment takes effect immediately. The Chairman is authorized to sign the letter of appointment and the contract deed. The Secretary is directed to communicate the decision to all chapters and to the Cooperative Federation office in Makurdi by 17th March.

The Board expressed appreciation to the Appointments Committee for their work and to Mr. Okafor for his service in the acting capacity.

4. FERTILIZER PROCUREMENT PLAN – 2021 WET SEASON
The GM (in attendance for this item) presented the procurement plan for the 2021 wet season:

- Total requirement: 2,400 bags (50kg each) of NPK 20:10:10
- Allocated to chapters: Ushongo 600, Logo 450, Guma 400, Vandeikya 350, Konshisha 300, Otukpo 300
- Estimated cost per bag: ₦9,500 (exclusive of transport)
- Total estimated cost: ₦22,800,000

The GM noted that the cooperative has secured a commitment from the Benue State Agricultural Development Authority for 1,200 bags at subsidized rate of ₦7,800 per bag. The remaining 1,200 bags will be purchased from open market.

Concerns raised:
- Mr. Sunday Oche asked about the payment schedule. The GM proposed 50% advance to the Authority upon signing, with balance on delivery. For open market purchases, a 30% deposit with the supplier (AgroPlus Limited, Makurdi) and the balance after inspection.
- Mrs. Grace Adanu asked about the quality verification. The GM said samples would be sent to the Federal Fertilizer Quality Control Laboratory in Jos before acceptance.
- Mr. Terkura Iorliam asked about the transport logistics. The GM confirmed that OVCU would use its two trucks plus hired vehicles. Transport cost estimated at ₦1,200 per bag for the farthest chapters.

The minutes of the Board meeting held on 18th March 2021 were circulated to all members prior to the meeting. It was moved by Mrs. Grace Adanu, seconded by Mr. Sunday Oche, that the minutes be adopted as a true record of the meeting. The motion was carried unanimously.

**2. MATTERS ARISING**

*2.1 Chapter visit report – February 2021*

The Chairman noted that the report on the chapter visits had been received and noted. Mr. Okafor's visit to the three chapters in February had resolved the seed distribution disputes, and no further complaints had been received from those chapters as at the end of March.

*2.2 Seed distribution – Logo chapter*

Mr. Iorliam raised a concern that the Logo chapter had not yet submitted their seed distribution reconciliation forms for the 2020 dry season. The GM said he would follow up with the Logo chapter chairman before 9th April. The Secretary was directed to send a reminder letter.

*2.3 Fertilizer procurement – previous season audit query*

The Chairman referred to the audit query raised by the external auditors regarding the 2020 fertilizer procurement. The Finance Officer had prepared a response which was tabled for discussion under Item 5.

---

**3. REPORT OF THE GENERAL MANAGER – CHAPTER VISITS AND SEED DISTRIBUTION**

The minutes record Fatima Bello's appointment_date as 2021-04-01. Record status: current.

(Continued from previous meeting – the GM had reported on the chapter visits and the resolution of seed distribution disputes.)

The GM added that the seed distribution for the 2021 dry season had been completed in all chapters except Konshisha, where 120 bags of maize seed remained undistributed due to a delay in the arrival of the seed from the supplier. The supplier, Benue Seeds Company, had promised delivery by 5th April. The GM said he would monitor the delivery and report to the Chairman.

No further discussion. The report was noted.

---

**4. FERTILIZER PROCUREMENT PLAN – 2021 WET SEASON (CONTINUED)**

The GM continued his presentation from the previous meeting. He noted that the plan had been circulated to all Board members and that the following additional points had been raised:

- The GM confirmed that the Benue State Agricultural Development Authority had verbally indicated that the 1,200 bags at the subsidized rate of ₦7,800 per bag would be available for collection from their Makurdi warehouse from 15th April. The Authority had asked for a formal letter of intent, which the GM had already drafted and forwarded on 30th March.

- Review of January activities: all scheduled trips and the Vandeikya workshop were completed. The mid-month progress report was submitted on Jan 12 as requested.
- Accounts Officer reported that January fuel spending came to N41,300 total, about N2,100 over the revised budget after the combined Gboko-Otukpo trip. The market run overage was the main cause. GM asked for a stricter fuel log for February, with the keke trips to be consolidated where possible.
- F/O Zone B raised that some societies are asking for the AGM date earlier than usual because of planting schedules. GM said the date is fixed for March 14 and will be confirmed at the February planning meeting. The notice will go out by Feb 20.
- Decision: draft AGM agenda to be prepared by Planning Desk by Feb 16 and circulated to the management committee for comments.

---

**Feb 7 – AGM Preparation Kickoff**

- Planning Desk began compiling the annual report for the AGM. Sections assigned: membership statistics (Planning), financial summary (Accounts), field activities (F/Os), and training/workshop outcomes (Planning).
- F/O Zone A to collect updated membership figures from all societies by Feb 20. F/O Zone C to follow up on any society that has not submitted.
- Venue for AGM: OVCU main hall, as in previous years. No change.
- Catering quotes to be obtained by Feb 15; Accounts to handle.

---

**Feb 9 – Vandeikya Workshop Follow-Up**

- F/O Zone C reported that 14 members from the workshop have since requested soil testing kits. The request was forwarded to the Benue State Agricultural Development Programme; they confirmed delivery of 20 kits by end of February.
- Planning Desk to schedule a short refresher session in March for Vandeikya members if the kits arrive on time.

---

**Feb 12 – Ushongo Credit Reminder**

- Accounts sent the reminder letter to Ushongo Cooperative Society per the Jan 15 decision, as the first installment of N50,000 had not been received by Jan 31.
- Chairman of Ushongo Cooperative Society called the Accounts Office on Feb 12 to say payment would be made by Feb 19. He asked for a small extension; Accounts noted this in the credit ledger. The remainder of N106,000 is still expected by March as agreed.
- GM noted that if the payment is not received by Feb 19, the matter should be escalated to the management committee.

---

**Feb 14 – AGM Draft Agenda Circulated**

- Planning Desk circulated the draft agenda for the March 14 AGM to the management committee. Items include:
  1. Opening and adoption of previous minutes
  2. Chairman's report
  3. Financial report and audited accounts
  4. Election of new committee members (3 positions)
  5. Fertilizer programme review for 2024
  6. Any other business
- Comments to be returned by Feb 21. Final agenda to be printed by Mar 1.

---

**Feb 15 – Catering Quotes Received**

- Accounts received three quotes for AGM refreshments:
  - Kwande Catering Services: N85,000
  - Mbaade Foods: N78,500
  - Tse-Agberagha Catering: N92,000
- Mbaade Foods quote is within budget; to be verified for capacity (expected attendance 120–150). Accounts to confirm by Feb 20.

---

**Feb 16 – Mid-February Progress Check**

- Planning Desk submitted the draft annual report sections for membership and training. Accounts to submit the financial summary by Feb 23.
- Membership figures collected so far: 14 of 22 societies have submitted updated numbers. Remaining societies to be followed up by F/Os by Feb 20.
- F/O Zone B reported that Lessel Cooperative Society has not submitted its membership update; the society's secretary said the list was being typed and would be sent by Feb 18.

documents.title: OVCU Monthly Planning Log
documents.content:
**OVCU Monthly Planning Log — April 2024 (continued)**

---

**Apr 15 – Quarterly Audit Scheduling**

- Planning Desk confirmed with the external auditors (Messrs. Aondo & Associates, Makurdi) that the audit for Q1 2024 will commence on **May 6** and run through May 10. The audit date was set after the auditors confirmed availability; the earlier tentative date of Apr 29 was moved because the auditors had a prior engagement in Katsina-Ala that week.
- Accounts to prepare the following for the audit team by May 2:
  1. Cash book and bank statements for Jan–Mar 2024
  2. Receipts and payment vouchers, filed by month
  3. Membership contribution schedules
  4. Fertilizer sales records and warehouse issue notes
  5. Asset register with depreciation schedule
- The audit clearance (unqualified opinion) is required before the AGM financial report can be presented. GM reminded the committee that the previous year's audit was completed in three days; this year's scope is larger, so the extra day has been built in.
- Planning Desk to book a meeting room at the OVCU office for the audit team, and arrange for tea/refreshments. Accounts to confirm the petty cash float for incidental audit expenses (not to exceed N5,000 without prior approval).
- The audit report is expected to be presented to the management committee by May 20, ahead of the June general meeting.

---

**Apr 15 – AGM Follow-Up**

- Minutes of the Mar 14 AGM were typed and circulated to all member societies by courier on Apr 8. Three societies (Mbaade, Tse-Agberagha, and Ushongo) have not yet confirmed receipt; F/Os to follow up this week.
- New committee members elected at the AGM were formally handed over on Apr 2. The outgoing committee submitted a handover note listing pending decisions, including the fertilizer programme review and the Ushongo credit follow-up.
- The fertilizer programme review was tabled at the AGM; members requested a detailed breakdown of distribution by society and by ward. Planning Desk to compile this from warehouse records and submit to the GM by Apr 25.

---

**Apr 16 – Ushongo Credit Status**

- Accounts confirmed that the Ushongo Cooperative Society paid the balance of N106,000 on **Apr 10**, clearing the outstanding credit. The earlier payment of N50,000 was received in February. Total credit of N156,000 is now fully settled.
- The credit ledger has been updated to show a zero balance for Ushongo. The society's chairman called to confirm receipt of the receipt and thanked the office for the extension.
- GM noted that the escalation agreed in February was not needed, and that the society's payment history should be noted as satisfactory for future credit requests.

---

**Apr 17 – Membership Updates (Final)**

- All 22 societies have now submitted their 2024 membership figures. Planning Desk consolidated the numbers and submitted the final summary to the GM on Apr 15. Total membership stands at 3,847 (up from 3,612 in 2023).
- Vandeikya Cooperative Society submitted the largest update (412 members); Lessel Cooperative Society submitted the smallest (98 members). The Lessel list was received on Apr 2, after two reminders.
- Planning Desk to prepare a one-page membership summary for the management committee meeting on Apr 24.

---

**Apr 18 – Training Kits Update**

- The training kits for Vandeikya members have not yet arrived. The supplier in Makurdi confirmed dispatch on Apr 3, but the courier company has not delivered. Planning Desk to call the courier today and request a tracking number.
- The refresher session scheduled for March was postponed; it will now be held on **May 15** at the Vandeikya Community Hall, subject to kit arrival. If the kits do not arrive by May 2, the session will be postponed again to June.
- F/O Zone A to confirm the venue booking and the expected attendance (target 60 members) by Apr 30.
